plan: A kirtan lit as call-and-response: the room learns a left-right hand-off in the intro, holds one lamp on the singer alone for eleven seconds, spends that hand-off properly when the congregation starts answering him at bar 31, and saves the only full-rig strobe in the show for the recording's own loudest half-second at 92.5s. Each section holds one colour so that the turns between them can be seen.

palette.note: Marigold saffron is the lead voice, temple-night indigo is the answer. Wherever two voices trade, those two colours trade with them - stated at moment 1 in the intro, spent at bars 31 and 36. Crimson belongs to section 3, the peak, and nowhere else; the last chorus comes back to saffron because the song's last word is devotional, not violent. Ember is the resting glow at both ends of the song. White is not a colour I place: it is where ramp whitens at the top of a build (bars 20-22 and 90-92.5s) and where the peak strobes. The full-rig hardware strobe is spent once, at 92.5s. Indigo is #3d55e0 rather than a deeper blue for a measured reason: at #1e2b8c it carried 0.20 relative luminance against saffron's 0.63, so every trade read as one half going dark rather than as two colours exchanging, and a bed in it left the groove at bar 15 dimmer than the intro.
palette.rig_grammar: The inner pair (par_8, par_15) is the voice; the outer pair (par_1, par_22) is the band. Where both are loud the two pairs are given different jobs - a bound pattern on one, a beat-locked bed on the other - so four lamps read as four lamps.

states.why: Bars 1-3 are the quietest in the song: 37/36/25% loud, 1-5 hits, lead-vocal and cello alone at 89bpm. Two centre lamps barely alive. The invocation is not a look, it is a held breath.

Anchored on moment 0: percussion 0.0 to 0.61, congas 0.0 to 0.39, and bar 4 jumps to 7 hits. One bump crosses the row per bar - the room starts moving. every_beats 4 rather than 1 on purpose: the song is at 89bpm here and a bump per beat would be flicker, not travel.
Moment 3, intensity 0.93, hold 13s: everything drops back behind the lead-vocal. This is the floor the isolate gesture stands on - near nothing, so one lamp can mean something.

Deliberately identical to the state before it. The boundary at 25.56s is a label, not an event: guitar is still at 0.05, strings at 0.04, and the singer is still alone. One look held for eleven seconds straight through a section seam is the stillest the show gets, and it is what makes bar 15 land.

Moment 4 is the gate: guitar 0.05 to 0.47, acoustic-guitar 0.02 to 0.35, strings 0.22 to 0.47, and bars 15-21 carry 11-13 onsets each. 0.05 to 0.46 in one step is the biggest state change so far. This bed travels once per bar on the outer pair while the accent binding takes the inner pair for the real drum hits.

Bars 23-29 run 67-78% with the whole band in (moment 6: six families at once, hold 15s). back-vocal is measured at exactly 0.00 across this entire stretch, so the leader is alone over the band and the room moves as one body. stagger 0.25 delays each lamp a quarter beat across the rig so the figure arrives left to right instead of four lamps in lockstep. One hue held for seventeen seconds, not two alternating: saffron is the leader, and he is the only voice in this half. drive swaps its two colours once per bar, which at this length is hue churn rather than an antiphon - the antiphon belongs to the trades, which hold a colour on each side of the room for seconds at a time.

back-vocal comes off zero at 65.5s and carries 66-82s. Same bed, colours swapped and the stagger nearly doubled - the room turns over and the figure sweeps harder across it from the moment the congregation joins. The lower floor leaves the trades room to read. Indigo held, answering the saffron half before it. The colour turn at bar 31 is the congregation arriving, and it is one change held across sixteen seconds instead of a swap every bar.

A held crimson core. This runs on the INNER pair only - the accent binding takes the ends - so two centre lamps burn steady while par_1 and par_22 snap on the real tom and kick hits (toms carry 82.5-95.5s peaking 1.0, kick at coverage 1.00). Deliberately the stillest bed in any loud section: all the motion here belongs to the ends, to the ramp climbing across it, and to the strobe it arrives at. Neither neighbour is a wash, so the loudest section does not look like the choruses on either side of it.

Bar 47 is the single loudest bar in the song at 92% but carries only 8 onsets - synth, kick, keys, digital-piano: a sustained plateau, not a drum section. So the highest floor in the show, the widest stagger, and no darkness between beats. The third chorus escalates by being fuller, not busier, and it is the one loud section with no binding on it so the grid holds the song's loudest passage. Both drive colours are the same saffron: the last chorus rests on one hue and escalates on level alone, so it reads as a held look rather than as the two-colour antiphon of section 2 repeated.

Moment 11 strips the track: back-vocal 0.58 to 0.04, snare 0.53 to 0.05, percussion, congas and toms gone, bar 53 down to 0 hits. 0.86 to 0.09 in a single move is the breakdown - it needs no gesture laid on top of it.

Strings, bass, guitar and acoustic-guitar all arrive together at moment 12 and stay. One colour, four lamps, nothing moving, for seven seconds. This is the show's rest - the last look was 0.42s of anything and the next one needs to be recognised, so this one is simply held.

The melody contour over 109-128s is measured rising, and violin, viola and bowed-strings all arrive at moment 14. The room starts travelling again, in saffron - back to the colour the intro opened in, at the same one-bump-per-bar rate.

Section 6's playing list is empty - the score hears silence here - and the final chord, E:7 from 125.74s, never resolves. Two centre lamps at an ember over an unresolved chord and no music. The show ends on the two lamps it started on.

bindings.why: Bars 15-21 carry 11-13 onsets each, the densest drumming outside the choruses. Inner pair only: the middle two lamps flash on the hits that were actually struck while the outer pair runs the travelling pulse bed. That is a bed and a pattern at once on a four-lamp rig, which is the only way to get texture here without all four moving as one. The isolate gesture overrides this back to darkness for the section's first seven seconds, which is why it can be declared section-wide. Flash colour and bed colour are the same indigo on purpose: the hit is a change of brightness, not of hue. Switching hue on every onset put the rig's colour churn above three changes a second, which is the thing a look has to survive to be recognised at all.

5.39 onsets per second across bars 40-48 - the busiest drumming in the song, and moment 8 is explicitly the drums thickening. The pairing is reversed from section 1 on purpose: here the ENDS catch the real tom and kick hits while the inner pair holds the breakdown grid, so the same idea returns wearing the other way round rather than repeating itself. Bed and flash are both crimson, so the ends punch brighter against the crimson core rather than changing colour six times a second. It leaves the whole of the loudest section in one hue - which is what makes the white at 92.5s the only colour event in it.

gestures.why: Moment 1 is an entrance and an exit on the same timestamp, which is trade's exact trigger: synth and back-vocal arrive (0.01 to 0.37, 0.06 to 0.30) while french-horn, lead-vocal, percussion, congas and cello all leave. Placed here at low stakes so the room's left-right hand-off and its two colours are established early - when the same figure returns at bar 31 for the congregation it is recognised, not introduced.

The tempo moves 89 to 119bpm and stays there, and bar 7 is the intro's loudest at 59% with back-vocal 0.23 to 0.69. The room steps up and holds. Not gear: gear lifts the whole rig six times a beat, which on a devotional intro would read as a fault in the rig rather than a change of pulse.

Moment 3: a spotlight on lead-vocal, intensity 0.93, holding 13 seconds. One warm lamp on the singer, the rest of the rig at 0.04, the head turned to face him, for eleven seconds - the longest single look in the show and the only time one lamp acts alone. On a symmetric row that normally reads as a fault; here the music is one voice, so it reads as the point.

Bar 13 is 55% loud with zero drum hits - vocal, lead-vocal and synth rising alone. One bloom inside the quietest eleven seconds of the show, so the spotlight is held rather than abandoned. The only swell in the plan.

Bars 19-21 are the top of the build - 63/61/68% loud with strings peaking 1.0 at 47s - and moment 5 is tagged alongside 'build'. Four beats short of two bars, climbing out of indigo to arrive exactly at the collapse. Two things measured against this plan shaped it: anticipation was here first and threw fifteen hard rig-lifts that landed nowhere near a beat, nineteen points of the show's beat alignment spent on one cue that is the wrong texture for a bhajan anyway; and ramp whitens and strobes at its top whatever `to` is set to, so it is kept short deliberately - long enough to be a riser, not long enough to rival 92.5s.

FULL DARK, 1 of 2. Bar 22 collapses to 39% straight after a 68% bar - guitar 0.77 to 0.13, bass 0.76 to 0.14, acoustic-guitar 0.59 to 0.05. The producer put the gap there; the room goes to nothing so that bar 23 has something to land on.
Bar 23 is 73% with kick, guitar and electric-guitar all in - the chorus arriving out of the dark. Saffron, not white: this is the devotional arrival, and white belongs to 92.5s alone.

The thesis of the show. Measured, not guessed: across 66-82s back-vocal runs 0.68/0.74/0.63 exactly where lead-vocal runs 0.34/0.08/0.03. back-vocal comes off zero right here and bar 31 jumps to 82%. One half of the room hands to the other - the leader calls, the congregation answers - and trade is the only effect in the catalogue that lights the whole rig while the lamps genuinely differ. (split would have said this more directly, but a binding covers a whole section, and back-vocal is silent for the first seventeen seconds of this one.)

The second exchange, five bars later: lead-vocal is back at 0.73/0.53/0.74 while back-vocal has fallen to 0.05/0.03/0.09. Colours reversed and shorter, so the leader takes it back. Two hand-offs, not a metronome - the repetition is the antiphon, which is the one figure in this song that is supposed to come round again.
Bar 38 drops to 50% between two bars above 85% - synth and vocal, a breath. The room quiets for exactly one bar so that the loudest stretch of the song arrives at bar 39 instead of merely continuing.

Moment 8 is the drums thickening (toms 0.17 to 0.39, kick 0.20 to 0.41) and bars 40-44 climb 79/83/82/89/88. Nine seconds of slow rise arriving exactly on the peak. The song climbs slowly here so the light climbs slowly; answering a long build with fast movement throws the build away. Climbing out of crimson rather than ramp's default blue, so the build stays inside the palette the loud plateau is painted in.

92.5s is the recording's own loudest half-second and moment 9's peak at intensity 1.0, sitting over G, the longest-held chord in the back half (90.00-95.83s). One second of hardware strobe at full white - the only white in the show and the brightest thing in it. Everything else is coloured so that this reads as the arrival it is.

Moment 10 thickens percussion, toms, congas, tambourine and flute, and the harmony turns A# to C across 101.4s. The ends only - the inner pair keeps the bed - so the third chorus gets its mid-section event without another full-rig flash nine seconds after the peak.

The last bar of the last chorus, spent once. Given the show's own four colours rather than the full hue wheel, so it turns through the palette as a flourish instead of reading as the rig faulting. It hands straight into the outro's collapse.

FULL DARK, 2 of 2, and the deeper one. Bar 54 is 12% loud with no lane loud enough for the score to name - the only true silence in the song. Four beats of nothing, ending exactly where strings, bass and guitar come back at moment 12.
The music moves up an octave and stays: violin 0.06 to 0.40, viola 0.04 to 0.25, bowed-strings 0.14 to 0.23. It rises and holds. Not a hit - nothing got louder, it went up.

The lead voice returns after being gone since 115.3s - lead-vocal and vocal both 0.0 to 0.45. Saffron on the inner pair: the same two lamps that held him alone at 21.8s, and the inner pair because the last stab hit the ends.

The beat drops away and strings, dobro, acoustic-guitar and guitar all fall from around 0.6 to 0.0 inside 2.5 seconds. A controlled pull-back that holds, not a cut - the band leaves, the room settles down to the ember it opened on, and the unresolved E:7 hangs over it.
